episodes.185846: Accumulated rainfall of up to around 3 to 4 inches over the San Sebastian Municipality in northwestern Puerto Rico served to saturate soils over the course of October 1st through 7th. Afternoon convection over northwestern Puerto Rico on October 9th where only up to 0.25 but served to trigger a mudslide.
episodes.186629: A stationary front across Southeast Florida led to the development of showers and thunderstorms, some with heavy rain, during the afternoon hours.
episodes.186719: Isolated waterspouts were observed near the lower and middle Florida Keys in association with scattered showers and thunderstorms developing along a decaying frontal boundary.
episodes.186748: An upper level moved out the Great Lakes towards New England on the 7th.  An area of low pressure developed across the Mid-Atlantic and pushed north into the Gulf of Maine through the day.  These features interacted with anomalous moisture across the region for  October bringing convective rain squalls and areas of heavy rain.  Most of Western Maine missed out on the heaviest of the rainfall but locally heavy rain begin to impact the Mid-Coast region by late afternoon.  The rain continued and became heavy at times through evening and into the night before tapering off by Midnight.  Coastal Knox County received the heaviest rainfall where close to 5 fell in some areas.

events.narrative: Heavy rain caused excessive run-off that caused Nickets Rd. from Ephraim Rd. to Black Rd. to close due to flooding.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A narrow waterspout was observed from area web cameras east of Duck Key.  The condensation funnel reached all the way to the water surface and a spray ring was visible.  The waterspout formed upshear but not connected to a long track, weak wall cloud.

events.county: Gulf Of Mexico From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To 5 Fathoms
events.narrative: A waterspout spray ring was posted on social media near a local business on Little Torch Key.

Reports of standing water 6-12 inches deep were reported in parts of Miami Beach as a result of afternoon thunderstorms producing brief, heavy rainfall. Rainfall amounts of up to 0.75 inches were estimated over a period of 1 hour.
Emergency Management reported a mudslide at PR-435 in Parcelas San Gabriel.
